chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, (on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal), from Abdullah Bakir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) [a gate which opens up to him] one thousand gates, each of which opens up to one thousand gates.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'thousand gates of knowledge' taught to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* illustrates the concept of *Ilm al-Imam* (the Imam's knowledge) as an infinite, hierarchical structure where the Prophet Muhammad imparted a foundational 'gate' of knowledge to Imam Ali, which itself contains a thousand sub-gates, each with a thousand more. This metaphor underscores the Shia belief in the Prophet's deliberate designation of Ali as the sole inheritor of his comprehensive spiritual and intellectual legacy, linking the Imams' authority directly to the Prophet's own divine instruction.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-25 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father, Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, (on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fazal), on the authority of Abdullah Bakir, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Aba Abdullah that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,
“Indeed God’s Prophet (MGB) taught Ali (MGB) a gate which opens up to one-thousand gates each of which would open up to another one-thousand gates.”
